I saved a revision checklist in Second Draft under your bus essay. It covers all nine comments and fits between the end of your shift and 11:45 p.m. English 110 allows AI help with planning, so the wording and submission are yours.

When you get home, start with the sentence in your conclusion proposing a one-year trial on routes 14 and 22. Move it into the opening and explain why the trial is worth trying. Your roommate’s forty-minute walk gives you a concrete place to start.

Your draft is 391 words, and the target is about 1,000. Spend most of your writing time on two questions: How much did ridership rise in Riverton, and where could the city get the money to cover lost fares on these routes? The checklist saves proofreading for last and leaves time for you to submit before 11:59 p.m.
